title: Direct Mapping: One Line per Block
unit: Memory Interfacing, Hierarchy and Cache Mapping
quickIdea: In a direct-mapped cache each memory block has exactly one home line: line = block number mod number of lines. One comparator decides the hit, and two blocks that share a home line evict each other forever.
remember: Line number = block number mod number of lines, which is the same as saying the index field of the address is the line number.
Hardware: one comparator per cache line, a tag store the width of one tag per line, and no replacement choice at all - the victim is decided by the address.
The hit time is the smallest of the three organisations: tag read, one compare, data out.
The cost is conflict misses: blocks that differ by a multiple of the number of lines cannot coexist even when most of the cache is empty.
The tag of a direct-mapped line identifies which of the (memory blocks / lines) blocks with that index is present, which is why its width is address width minus log2(lines) minus offset.

example.prompt: A 2 KB direct-mapped cache has 64 B blocks. Which line holds the byte at address 0xA248, and what is its tag?
example.answer: Line 9, tag 20, offset 8 - the split GATE CSE 2022 Q.44 uses for P and S.

gateAngle: GATE's direct-mapping questions come in three shapes: give the fields, give the line for an address, or give a reference sequence and ask which block survives. All three are the modulo and the tag compare.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: GATE CSE 2019 Q.1 asks for the tag and index widths of a 16 kB fully associative cache with 16 B blocks. How does the direct-mapping formula specialise to it?
variations.answer: Fully associative means one set, so index = 0; offset = log2 16 = 4 and tag = 32 - 4 = 28 bits.
variations.why: It shows the three organisations as one formula: direct is 1 way, fully associative is all ways, and the index field is log2 of the number of sets in both.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: An 8-line direct-mapped cache holds blocks 0, 8, 16 and 24 in turn, then re-reads 0. How many misses in the five accesses?
variations.answer: Five: all four blocks map to line 0, so each evicts the previous one and the re-read of 0 misses.
variations.why: It is the conflict-miss pattern in its purest form, and it is the shape GATE CSE 2022 Q.44 uses with two blocks.

trap.what: Thinking a direct-mapped cache wastes space only when it is full.
trap.why: A conflict miss happens while most lines are empty; capacity is irrelevant to it.
trap.counterexample: A 32-line direct-mapped cache holding only blocks 0 and 32: both map to line 0, so alternating accesses miss every time and 31 lines stay empty.

check.question: A direct-mapped cache has 128 lines and 16 B blocks. To which line does byte address 0x1234 map, and what is the offset?
check.explanation: The low 4 bits are the offset because the block is 16 bytes; the next 7 bits are the line.

sourceLine: Direct mapping as one line per set with conflict misses as its characteristic cost: IISc CDS slides (English, read in part). Line = block mod total lines, with the warning that it is modulo and not division: DSWallah Learn, romanised Hindi, translated (read in part). Direct-mapped caches treated as the base case for misses, writes and performance: NPTEL IIT Guwahati Lecture 25 (English, read in part). The 2022 sequence is simulated in scripts/validate.py.
